title: What shape is Nepal’s flag? Meet the double pennant

sources.name: Government of Nepal — Constitution, Article 8 and Schedule 1 (PDF)

practice: Look for the shape, colours and symbols in World Flags.

sections.html:
Nepal’s flag is a double pennant: two joined triangular shapes, one above the other. A straight edge runs beside the flagpole; two points face outwards. No, nobody has cropped a rectangle.

In a flag quiz, that outline is your first clue. Look at the shape before the colours.
sections.title: The outline is the first clue

sections.html:
The main field is crimson, edged in deep blue. A white moon sits above a white sun. Article 8 of Nepal’s Constitution describes the design.

Which symbol goes at the top? The moon. That little detail is easier to remember than a whole flag at once.
sections.title: Two colours, two sky clues

sections.html:
Here is the unexpected part: Schedule 1 gives instructions for drawing the flag, including its outline, moon, sun and border.

There are distances to mark and arcs to construct. It is more precise than “draw two triangles and hope for the best”.

The construction lines are guides, not extra marks on the finished flag. Think of the faint pencil work behind a drawing.
sections.title: The constitution includes the drawing instructions

sections.html:
Try the same approach with other flags: outline, layout, then one distinctive symbol. Three small clues beat one large blur.

Our guide to learning world flags has more examples. With Nepal, start around the edge.
sections.title: Try looking at shape before colour

description: Two joined triangles, a moon and a sun: spot Nepal’s double-pennant flag and discover the drawing instructions hidden in its constitution.
